_why: WHICH PERSON EACH DIRECT-LINE GENERATION IS, so a person page can draw its
own family instead of the family filed under its name.
WHY THIS IS NEEDED AND WHY IT IS ONLY EIGHT ROWS. The kin in this archive
is attached to a NAME, in dossiers.json's `people`, keyed by name-slug.
roster.json carries the 1,440 pids and no kin at all. So when the name
page was split into a name index and a person page, the photographs went
to the person and the family tree stayed on the name — on the page that
now says «This is a NAME, not a person».
AND THE NAME-KEYED TREES CANNOT SIMPLY BE MOVED. /who/ivan-defranceski/
holds a `ptree` whose `self` reads «Ivan Defranceski, 1829 – 1895» and
whose spouse is CHERYL LERENA and whose child is DAVID — one man's dates,
another man's wife, a third man's son, on one page. Three Ivan
Defranceski share that name-slug: 1925, 1943 and 1951. Attaching that
tree to a person page would publish the composite as a person's family.
Of 456 name-page trees, only 44 identify themselves well enough to be
matched to one person — their own `self` states a birth year that one
roster row shares. 324 state no year at all. That is the measure of how
far the kin is from being person-level.
directline.json IS person-level and ordered, so the eight generations of
the direct line can be drawn correctly and are. Everyone else's person
page says plainly that this archive records kin by name, and links to the
name index rather than inventing a family for them.
Built 23 September 2026. Rebuild it by matching each generation's name and
birth year against roster.json; it is not derived at page-render time on
purpose, so a reader can see which person each generation is.
